title: Louis Armstrong as a boy: charcoal, jail and learning trumpet
summary: Williams describes Louis as a bad boy who sold charcoal, was jailed, and learned trumpet there.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: What was he like before he took out traffic? Was he playing anything else?

No, well, you see, Lewis was a kind of bad boy, you know. See, he first was out of one thing, then another. Used to sell charcoal, had charcoal schooners on the old New Basin Canal. I guess you heard about that. But he was selling charcoal out there, you know. As a kid, you know, see. Well, he wouldn't go to school. And they would pick him up and put him in jail, you know, juvenile delinquency. You know, see. The last time they put Lewis in jail, it kept him in there for indefinite legacy. Well, that's how he learned how to play the trumpet, too. Come right out the way of his home playing the trumpet. No one wasn't reading, you know. Mr. Dave tried to learn the music, but he, you know, he couldn't.
